queries.query: LLM-generated network configuration failures OR incorrect network config OR unsafe NetOps changes
queries.rationale: Directly locate empirical and case studies documenting the phenomenon: incorrect, unsafe, or nonfunctional network configurations produced by generative models or automated agents.

queries.query: intent-to-configuration translation "natural language" to network configuration OR intent-driven NetOps using LLMs
queries.rationale: Find work on mapping operator intent (NL) to concrete configs, task formulations, datasets, and failure modes specific to NetOps.
source_preferences: Network operator blogs (NANOG) and vendor docs

queries.rationale: Investigate underlying mechanisms that make LLMs produce incorrect assertions (mechanistic explanations relevant to NetOps risk).
source_preferences: Technical blog posts from major labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind)

queries.rationale: Survey generate–validate–repair pipelines and verifier-assisted correction approaches applicable to network configs.

queries.query: formal verification network configurations "model checking" "SMT" "header space analysis" NetOps verification tools
queries.rationale: Locate deterministic/verifiable validators and formal-analysis tools used to check forwarding, reachability, and policy compliance.

queries.query: constrained generation controlled generation LLMs "safety filters" "prompt constraints" "RLHF" for operations
queries.rationale: Capture techniques to constrain or steer generation to safer outputs (fine-tuning, RLHF, constrained decoding, templates).

queries.query: tool-assisted LLMs for operations "tool use" "external verifier" "sandboxed execution" agent frameworks NetOps
queries.rationale: Find architectures where LLMs call tools (validators, emulators, CLIs) to improve reliability in operational workflows.

queries.query: benchmarks LLM for AIOps NetOps "benchmark" "dataset" "limitations" "external validity"
queries.rationale: Identify existing benchmarks/datasets for LLMs in networking/AIOps and literature critiquing their validity/realism.

queries.query: empirical evaluations LLM reliability in code generation configuration synthesis "evaluation methodology"
queries.rationale: Survey empirical methodologies used to evaluate LLMs on program/config generation tasks and how they measure correctness and safety.

queries.query: adversarial prompts "prompt injection" "prompt attacks" robustness LLMs operational tasks
queries.rationale: Locate work on adversarial inputs and prompt-based attacks that degrade LLM reliability in operational contexts.

queries.query: simulators and testbeds for NetOps experiments "Mininet" "ns-3" "emulation" containerized network testbeds for automated configuration testing
queries.rationale: Identify practical execution/evaluation environments and their pros/cons for validating generated configs safely.

queries.query: metrics for operational correctness NetOps "reachability tests" "policy compliance" "connectivity matrix" "semantic correctness"
queries.rationale: Collect concrete metrics used to evaluate whether a generated configuration meets operational requirements.

queries.query: guarded agentic workflows safety "agentic AI" netops orchestration "guard rails" "rollback"
queries.rationale: Explore agent orchestration patterns that include safety guards, rollback, staged deployment, or approvals for NetOps agents.

queries.query: human-in-the-loop verification for automated NetOps "operator approval" "human oversight" workflow
queries.rationale: Survey designs that integrate operator oversight and decision checkpoints to mitigate automated agent mistakes.

queries.query: surveys and systematic reviews LLMs for AIOps NetOps "survey" "systematic review"
queries.rationale: Gather broad-positioning and prior-art syntheses to map the field and identify literature gaps.

queries.query: accountability auditability agentic operations "explainability" "audit trails" NetOps automation
queries.rationale: Find work on auditability, logging, and explainability required for safe, accountable automated network changes.

queries.query: statistical methods for model comparison "paired design" bootstrap McNemar test confidence intervals for reliability studies
queries.rationale: Collect appropriate statistical techniques and best practices for evaluating model reliability and paired comparisons in experiments.

inclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed publications (conferences, journals) and reputable preprints (arXiv) relevant to LLMs, NetOps, AIOps, verification, or agentic systems.
Practical engineering reports, open-source project documentation, or operator forum posts that describe real-world NetOps tooling or incidents (NANOG, vendor whitepapers).
Works that present empirical data, methods, or reproducible artifacts (code, datasets, testbeds) for evaluation of configuration correctness, verification, or agentic workflows.
Papers and reports from 2018–2026, with priority on 2020–2026 for LLM-specific content; earlier seminal works on formal verification or network verification are acceptable.
exclusion_criteria: Purely promotional marketing materials lacking methods or data (vendor marketing slides without technical detail).

Non-technical blog posts or social-media content without supporting technical documentation or reproducible artifacts, except official engineering blogs from major research labs when they include technical detail.

Papers outside the scope of NetOps/AIOps or generic NLP model description without application or relevance to network operations (e.g., generic language-model benchmarks unrelated to config or operational actions).
Proprietary datasets or closed-access artifacts that cannot be inspected or reproduced by researchers using public resources.
Works in languages other than English unless an authoritative English translation or extended abstract is available.
date_rationale: Prioritize recent work (2020–2026) because large pretrained LLMs and agentic tool-use techniques matured after 2020; include 2018–2019 for foundational network-verification and formal-methods literature. Emphasize the newest papers (2022–2026) for agentic/LLM-in-operations developments, while retaining seminal earlier sources for verification, testing, and operational practices.
